corrections.compiler_and_flags: simdxml/sxq: cargo build --release, workspace [profile.release] lto=true, codegen-units=1, strip=true (rustc version not stated; MSRV 1.75). pugixml side: bench/pugixml-xpath.cpp shim built with `c++ -O2 -std=c++17` against the system libpugixml (bench/run-x86.sh; the author's blog says pugixml 1.14 at -O2). corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from the project's own README and bench scripts; not independently reproduced. The end-to-end CLI comparisons favor sxq. sxq parses files over 1 MB in parallel on all cores by default, while the pugixml shim is single-threaded. For DBLP, and for the PubMed //MeshHeading query in run-x86.sh, sxq runs with -c (prints only the match count) while the pugixml shim extracts and prints the text of every match. So the 2.6x DBLP and 1.3x PubMed figures compare multi-threaded count-only output against single-threaded full text output. The README and the author's blog say pugixml wins count() and contains() queries (blog: 0.88x and 0.91x). No rustc or C++ compiler version stated. The repo has no LICENSE file: MIT OR Apache-2.0 is declared only in Cargo.toml and the README, and GitHub reports no license. 14 stars; last main commit 2026-03-27.

notes: All README numbers match the record. Downgraded A to C under the no-compiler-version rule. The CLI method also favors sxq (all-core parallel parse plus count-only output against a single-threaded pugixml printing text). A web search turned up a C++23 port, KrzysztofKowalski/libsimdxml, which may be worth a separate look for the C++-first list; I did not evaluate it.

corrections.claimed_speedup: vs libxml2 (README, Apple Silicon): SAX 2.5x (~1 KB) and 3.6x (~5 KB), DOM parse 1.4x (~5 KB), attribute lookup 1.9x, text extraction 2.6x, indexed child access 9% faster, XPath 1.3-4.0x on all 10 listed queries (several libxml2 cells are approximate, '~1 us'/'~3 us'). vs pugixml: attribute-set ~25x (measured against an approximate '~8-14 ms find+set' pugixml figure), serialize attr-heavy 2 MB 1.6x faster, but 1.3x slower on 10k-child append and 1.1x slower on text-heavy serialize.
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers; not independently reproduced. No CPU model or compiler version, and libxml2 and pugixml are unversioned system/Homebrew builds. The libxml2 XPath harnesses call xmlXPathEvalExpression, which re-parses the expression on every call, while leptris evaluates through its internally cached compiled expressions, so the XPath ratios include libxml2's per-call compile. No published benchmark produces the pugixml '~8-14 ms (find+set)' figure behind the ~25x attribute-set claim: benchmarks/matrix/bench_matrix.cpp, the harness the README cites, times pugixml append_attribute with no find. The project's latest macOS CI artifact (Benchmark run 36132268169, v1.9.243, macos-latest) shows smaller margins than the README (derived): SAX small ~2.1x, SAX medium ~1.3x (README 3.6x), XPath attribute::id ~1.7x CPU time (README 4.0x), descendant::* ~1.6x CPU time and parity on wall time. License conflict: LICENSE.md is a Ribose BSD-2-Clause text, while the README, the Ruby gemspec, the Rust Cargo.toml and vcpkg.json say MIT (both are OSI-approved). Repo created Nov 2025, 1 star, very active (v1.9.243); same org as teptris and yeptris.

notes: Downgraded B to C: benchmarks in the project's own repo are C under the rubric, since B needs a paper or an independent suite. The numbers match the README. But no harness produces the pugixml figure behind the ~25x claim, and the project's current CI shows smaller libxml2 margins than the README. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION; LICENSE.md is BSD-2-Clause, so I kept that and recorded the MIT conflict in caveats.
